advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure scan_and_write_unlinks reports already-written UNLINK paths to the caller's rollback set even when a later _write_unlink raises the write-gate CommandError (e.g., accumulate into a caller-visible list or wrap the scan so partial writes are cleaned up).
evidence: delete.py:145: `    written: list[str] = []` (local accumulator, only returned on success)
delete.py:156/164: `p = _write_unlink(... repo_root)` inside the per-source loop can now raise CommandError via finalize_event's write-gate

delete.py:319-320: `unlink_paths = scan_and_write_unlinks(...)` then `written.extend(...)` — the caller's rollback set is populated only AFTER the scan returns, so a mid-scan raise loses already-written paths

_seam.py:319-325: the write-gate exemption is decided per-event via `_event_ticket_type(ticket_id,...)` which reduces the SOURCE ticket, so exemption can differ between source tickets — an exempt session_log source (writes its UNLINK) can precede a non-exempt task source (raises)
advisory.finding: scan_and_write_unlinks accumulates written UNLINK paths in a local list that is only returned to the caller on success; if a later _write_unlink raises the require_authenticated write-gate CommandError, earlier UNLINK files already written to other tickets' directories are not captured in the caller's `written`/`unlink_paths` and therefore are NOT rolled back, leaking events on disk.
scenarios: Deleting a ticket that has inbound LINKs from BOTH an exempt source (session_log/code_review/identity) and a non-exempt source, under identity.require_authenticated with no resolvable signing identity: the exempt source's UNLINK is written to disk, then the non-exempt source triggers the gate and raises, leaving the first UNLINK file uncommitted but on disk and un-rolled-back.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have _delete_cli pass its `written` list into scan_and_write_unlinks (or catch the CommandError inside scan_and_write_unlinks, appending partial paths before re-raising) so the existing unstage+remove rollback covers UNLINKs written before the gate refusal.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a deleted ticket's STATUS(deleted)/ARCHIVED (and any UNLINK) events carry author_sig via the shared finalize seam.
evidence: Test docstring names delete: 'The transactional write path (transition / claim / close, and delete) must sign its STATUS / EDIT events' (test file line 3)
search for 'delete' in tests/unit/test_identity_txn_signing_heldout.py returned no matches
delete.py line 238: 'finalize_event(event, tkt_id, event_type, data, tkt_tracker, repo_root)' for STATUS/ARCHIVED events; line 131 for UNLINK
delete.py lines 340-345 write STATUS(deleted) and ARCHIVED through _write_event via repo_root — the new signing path
advisory.finding: The delete write path — newly routed through finalize_event to sign UNLINK / STATUS(deleted) / ARCHIVED events (delete.py _write_unlink line 131, _write_event line 238) — has NO test verifying those delete events are signed, even though the commit message and the test file's own docstring name 'and delete' as part of the signing contract. A regression where delete silently skips the seam and writes unsigned STATUS/ARCHIVED events (breaking require_authenticated on any deleted ticket's history) would pass the whole suite undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor drops repo_root or the finalize_event call from delete.py; deleted tickets write unsigned events; the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_delete_events_are_signed(signed_repo): create a ticket (and a linking ticket to force an UNLINK), delete it, then read the STATUS(deleted)/ARCHIVED/UNLINK events off disk and assert all(e.get('author_sig')).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that deletes a ticket under require_authenticated with no signable identity and asserts the delete is refused AND no STATUS/ARCHIVED/UNLINK/tombstone files remain on disk (clean rollback).
evidence: delete.py lines 312-315 comment: 'On failure, roll back the specific files this delete wrote'
delete.py lines 354-368: except CommandError: ... git reset ... os.remove(p) ... return exc.returncode
finalize_event raises CommandError 'ONLY when identity.require_authenticated is on and a NON-exempt event cannot be signed' (_seam.py lines 340-342)
search for 'delete' in the test file returned no matches — no delete refusal/rollback test exists
advisory.finding: The delete rollback contract introduced by this change is untested. Because _write_event now raises CommandError mid-operation under require_authenticated (delete.py line 238), the except-CommandError block (lines 354-368) that unstages and removes every already-written file must run to avoid a half-deleted, wedged-on-rerun store. No test injects an unsignable delete under enforcement to force that recovery path — unlike the transition case which IS covered by test_unsignable_transition_is_refused_under_enforcement.
scenarios: require_authenticated on, no signable identity, delete a ticket: after a first UNLINK/STATUS write, _write_event raises; the rollback must remove written files so the store is unchanged and a re-run is not wedged.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror test_unsignable_transition_is_refused_under_enforcement for delete: create a ticket with enforcement off, set REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1, invoke delete, assert it fails and that no new event files or .tombstone.json were written for the ticket.
